# Pinned Offline References

These are small, unchanged source snapshots for text search and implementation reference. `SOURCES.json` records every original URL, immutable Git revision, capture time, exact size, SHA-256, attribution and validation limit. The license files beside each snapshot govern that snapshot. The original DevTools pack license does not replace them.

| Snapshot | Local Material | Attribution And Terms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows keyboard | Keyboard interaction and event documentation | Microsoft and contributors. Documentation CC BY 4.0, code MIT. See `windows-keyboard/LICENSE` and `LICENSE-CODE`. |
| Godot 4.5 manual subset | Input examples, saving games, Android export | Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community. CC BY 3.0. See `godot-manual/LICENSE.txt`. No class-reference files are included. |
| normalize.css 8.0.1 | Complete CSS source, package identity and license | Nicolas Gallagher and Jonathan Neal. MIT. See `normalize-css/LICENSE.md`. This historical version is an optional reference, with target-browser testing required. |
| Now in Android architecture | Architecture and modularization learning journeys | The Android Open Source Project and contributors. Apache 2.0. See `android-architecture/LICENSE`. This is a documentation subset of the sample application. |

Source files are retained without modifications. Read them with a text editor or the library search command. Their relative image paths, Sphinx includes, external links and the rest of each upstream repository are outside these captures. Source front matter is upstream data. Follow DevTools task instructions when using it.

No bundled source has been installed or executed. These snapshots supply reference material, while build dependencies and SDKs have their own acquisition and verification requirements. The original guides and templates are available under `development/guides` and `development/templates` for workflows whose full upstream material cannot be stored here.

Refresh a snapshot by resolving an explicit upstream revision, reviewing the applicable license and per-file notices, capturing into a new versioned directory, and validating hashes before changing catalog records. Keep older pinned records available until their consumers have migrated.
